nodes.content: Design a typed Rust–JavaScript FFI preserving Rust aliasing guarantees across asynchronous callbacks, cancellation, and garbage collection.
requirements: Establish memory safety through explicit boundary semantics covering reentrancy, cancellation, and JavaScript-retained Rust objects.
Achieve ≤20% callback latency overhead versus equivalent handwritten unsafe bindings on a declared benchmark suite.

nodes.content: Generate typed, generation-tagged handles with fast-path borrow leases, queued reentrant callbacks, cancellation-owned tasks, and GC reclamation after leases end.
When may JavaScript reenter, cancel, or collect a handle while Rust holds an active mutable lease?
Deferring reentrant callbacks, cancellation drops, and GC reclamation until lease release yields zero alias violations in JSLeaseStress-1.
Specify lease-state transitions for reentry, cancellation, and GC; implement wasm-bindgen handles; run JSLeaseStress-1 and CallbackBench.
Run JSLeaseStress-1 for 100,000 seeded callback/cancellation schedules under Node --expose-gc, logging lease overlaps and stale-handle accesses.
JSLeaseStress-1: 100,000 seeded schedules, zero overlapping leases or stale-handle dereferences; 8,412 cancellation/GC drops deferred until lease release.
Adopt lease-release deferral for reentry and destruction; JSLeaseStress-1 found no alias violations, pending broader safety and latency validation.
Implement wasm-bindgen wrappers with generation-checked handles, queued reentry, cancellation tombstones, and FinalizationRegistry-triggered lease-safe cleanup.
lease-ffi v0.1 contains generated scoped-borrow wrappers, generation-checked JS handles, reentry queues, and cancellation/GC cleanup code.
Benchmark CallbackBench’s sync, Promise, cancellation, and GC paths under Node 22; compare lease-ffi v0.1 median latency against handwritten unsafe bindings.
CallbackBench Node 22 median overhead versus unsafe bindings: sync 12%, Promise 15%, cancellation 17%, GC 19%; all ≤20%.
Run Miri host-shim borrow checks and 50,000 Node 22 forced-GC traces on lease-ffi v0.1, including reentry and cancellation.
Three of 50,000 forced-GC traces freed handle slots before queued callbacks checked generations; Miri reproduced use-after-free.
How can queued callbacks pin handle slots through forced GC while retaining CallbackBench overhead at ≤20%?
Prototype enqueue-time slot pins released after callback completion; rerun Miri, forced-GC traces, and CallbackBench against 19% GC overhead.
Enqueue-time pins eliminated use-after-free across 50,000 forced-GC traces and Miri, but raised CallbackBench GC overhead from 19% to 24%.
Retain enqueue-time pins for safety, but defer release until GC-path overhead falls from 24% to ≤20%.
Use event-loop-local queue-owned retain flags instead of per-callback pins; reclaim slots after lease and queue drain, targeting ≤20% overhead.
Can queue-owned retain flags prevent premature reclamation and slot reuse while keeping GC-path callback overhead ≤20%?
Queue-owned retain flags prevent premature slot reclamation across 50,000 forced-GC traces while keeping CallbackBench GC overhead ≤20%.
Implement queue-owned retain flags; rerun Miri, 50,000 forced-GC traces, and Node 22 CallbackBench against pinned and unsafe baselines.
Queue-owned flags passed Miri and 50,000 forced-GC traces without premature reclamation; CallbackBench GC overhead fell to 18% versus unsafe.
Adopt queue-owned retain flags: Miri and 50,000 forced-GC traces passed, with 18% GC callback overhead versus unsafe bindings.
Generate typestate wrappers from a model-checked boundary protocol, restricting borrowed callbacks and enforcing cancellation/GC ownership at runtime.
Can typestate-generated wrappers reject borrows spanning awaits while safely transferring callback, cancellation, and GC ownership?
Typestate wrappers reject all 40 BorrowAcrossAwait compile-fail cases, while ownership transfers remain violation-free across 50,000 GC/cancellation traces.
Model-check the lease protocol, generate typestate wrappers, then run 40 BorrowAcrossAwait compile-fail cases and 50,000 GC/cancellation traces.
BorrowAcrossAwait rejected 39/40 cases; an async closure captured a mutable lease across await despite typestate generation.
Run 50,000 seeded GC/cancellation traces with Miri, checking typestate ownership transfers and queue-owned retain flags for double-free.
Miri found zero double-frees or ownership violations across 50,000 seeded GC/cancellation traces with queue-owned retain flags.
How should generated callback signatures prevent async closures from capturing a mutable lease across await?
Preserve Miri-validated ownership transfers; require higher-ranked synchronous lease closures and owned async futures, then rerun BorrowAcrossAwait and GC/cancellation traces.
lease-ffi v0.2 adds higher-ranked synchronous lease callbacks, owned async futures, and queue-owned retain flags.
Gate lease-ffi v0.2 on borrow compile-fail tests, cancellation/reentry/GC stress, and ≤20% per-path CallbackBench overhead.
Does lease-ffi v0.2 reject all cross-await borrows, survive reentry/cancellation/GC stress, and meet ≤20% CallbackBench overhead per path?
lease-ffi v0.2 rejects 40/40 BorrowAcrossAwait cases, passes 100,000 reentry/GC/cancellation schedules, and stays ≤20% overhead on every CallbackBench path.
Run compile-fail, Miri and Node forced-GC stress, then benchmark four CallbackBench paths against handwritten unsafe bindings.
Execute 40 BorrowAcrossAwait compile-fail cases and 100,000 seeded Node 22 reentry/cancellation/forced-GC schedules against lease-ffi v0.2.
lease-ffi v0.2 rejected 40/40 cross-await borrows; 100,000 seeded reentry/cancellation/forced-GC schedules found zero alias violations or stale-handle dereferences.
Run Miri host-shim checks and measure lease-ffi v0.2 CallbackBench median latency across four Node 22 paths versus unsafe bindings.
Miri host-shim checks passed; CallbackBench v0.2 median overhead versus unsafe: sync 13%, Promise 16%, cancellation 18%, GC 19%.
Does CallbackBench’s 19% GC-path median overhead remain ≤20% across repeated Node 22 runs with forced GC?
Across 30 independent Node 22 CallbackBench runs, the GC-path median overhead stays ≤20% in every run.
Repeat CallbackBench GC-path measurements in 30 isolated Node 22 processes, recording per-run median overhead and forced-GC counts.
All 30 GC-path medians were ≤20% (maximum 19.9%); run 17 exposed a post-measurement stale-handle dereference during forced GC.
Which queue-drain and forced-GC ordering allowed run 17’s post-measurement stale-handle dereference despite queue-owned retain flags?
Capture run 17’s event order, minimize the failing schedule, inspect slot reclamation versus callback dequeue, and rerun Miri.
Replay run 17 against the passing Miri baseline; log GC, queue-drain, and slot-reuse events, then test a minimized schedule.
Minimized replay reproduced run 17: dequeue cleared the retain flag before scheduling callback execution; forced-GC cleanup reclaimed its slot.
Block v0.2 release; retain queue ownership through callback completion, then repeat forced-GC replay, safety stress, and latency checks.
Extend queue-owned retention through callback completion; replay run 17, rerun Miri and 100,000 reentry/cancellation/forced-GC schedules, then benchmark CallbackBench.
lease-ffi v0.3 retains queued handles through callback completion and defers GC slot reclamation until ownership releases.
